title: Dummy bcrypt compare on unknown username prevents timing oracle on username existence
description: credentials.rs always runs a bcrypt comparison even when the username is not found (comparing against a precomputed dummy hash). This ensures the AUTHINFO USER/PASS round-trip takes approximately the same wall time whether the username exists or not, preventing an attacker from enumerating valid usernames via timing. A contributor might remove this as a 'pointless comparison on a None path' or as dead code when the user is not found. It is neither — it is a deliberate constant-time property. Defend: without the dummy compare, a timing measurement of ~1ms (user not found, fast path) vs ~100ms (user found, bcrypt computes) leaks the username set.
